about: Ground plan for the north-pool area (docs/SMOOTH_PATHS.md, drawn by src/ground-plan.ts, checked by scripts/check_ground_plan.py). World metres: x east, z south.
trust: The crazy-paving path is the photo-traced band from data/north_pool_gardens.json (IMG_2204-2206, 2208), now a smooth centreline. The lawn is bounded by that path, Calle Isabel and the dark hedge line the aerial shows on the south; the deck is cut out of it. Edges good to about a metre.

surfaces.name: North pool lawn
surfaces.note: IMG_2204 and IMG_2205 (solved station camera) show lawn all round the pool deck. Its north and west sides follow the crazy-paving path's pool-side edge, its east side Calle Isabel, its south side the two hedges, both cast through the camera (2026-11-15). The aerial's dark band south of these hedges was the hedges themselves, read as grass, so the earlier aerial trace ran 3-5 m too far south. What lies south of the hedges is not seen. The measured deck is cut out. Good to about half a metre near the camera, a metre on the north side. 2026-11-15: the north edge moved 0.8-2.7 m north to the grass edge photographed in IMG_2205 (cast through its solved camera), between the deck and the path.

edges.note: The long clipped hedge closing the lawn's south side (IMG_2204 foreground, IMG_2205 lower right): its lawn-side top edge cast through the solved camera at 0.9 m runs from (-175.3, 29.8) to (-168.2, 25.7); east of the photo's edge to the yucca by Calle Isabel it is estimated. Height and depth by eye.

The hibiscus hedge at the lawn's south-west corner (IMG_2204, pink flowers), with a low white kerb along its lawn side cast through the solved camera at ground level from (-180.1, 28.2) to (-177.9, 28.5); its south and west extent run out of the photo and are estimated.
The thin white kerb along the hibiscus hedge's lawn side (IMG_2204).

surfaces.name: North pool · crazy-paving lawn-edge path
surfaces.note: Photo-supported: irregular pale stone paving follows the curved retaining frontage at the northwest and the lower plinths across the north side, flush with the lawn (IMG_2204-2206, 2208). Estimated: 0.96 m width and exact plan curve (about +-2 m registration). Moved 2026-11-14 from data/north_pool_gardens.json as the centreline of its traced band. IMG_2204 shows the paving continuing down the west side along the curved white wall and along the south side behind the hedges; those continuations are not traced yet (task ground-plan-north-pool). 2026-11-15, through the solved IMG_2204 camera (pixels on the paving cast onto the surveyed ground): the west side runs at the foot of the curved white wall, about 1.4 m east of the earlier band (which projected onto the wall top); at the south-west corner it runs east to the tip of the hibiscus hedge and turns south along the hedge's west side out of view (stones at the photo's lower left); a second short path leaves the lawn south through the gap between the hibiscus hedge and the long south hedge. The north stretch is kept against the north patio fronts: cast through the same camera it lands 1-3 m further north, which would put it inside the patios (and the tree beside it casts 2 m north of where it stands against the paving), so the camera's far casts are taken as off and this is an open discrepancy, not a correction. 2026-11-15, re-traced with the north patios through the solved IMG_2205 camera (IMG_2204 as cross-check): the north stretch runs at the foot of the plinth wall, 0.7-2.4 m north of where it was, with the lawn's north edge at the photographed grass edge; this resolves the earlier north discrepancy (the patio fronts it was kept against were themselves traced too far south). Width 1.3 m for the whole path (the north side measures about 1.1-1.7 m between wall foot and grass).

surfaces.name: Calle Isabel's crazy-paving surface beside the north pool lawn
surfaces.note: IMG_2205 (solved station camera) shows the lane down the east side of the lawn paved in the same irregular stone as the lawn-edge path, not terracotta tiles: its west edge, cast through the camera onto the surveyed ground, runs at x -165.9 from z 9.5 to 18 (within 0.3-0.6 m of the mapped lane's west edge), and it reappears beyond the yucca bending south-east (about -163.8, 21.8 to -163.3, 22.6). The east edge is hidden by the yucca, so the surface takes the mapped lane's paved width with its margin (1.32 m), raised 0.21 m to lie just over the lane's own tiles (lanes are drawn 0.27 m over the ground). The lane's line and level stay those of data/street_layout.json; this is its surface. 15 Nov: the south bend moved about 0.5 m east so the yucca, whose trunk base casts to (-164.2, 22.5), stands on the lawn at the lane's edge as in IMG_2205.

surfaces.name: North pool · walled patio with two brown gates south of the west path
surfaces.note: Photo-supported (IMG_2206, IMG_2208): a terracotta-tiled patio with a parasol, held by two white walls about 1.7-1.9 m high with curved cappings and brown plank gates, bougainvillea and plumbago over them. Measured through the solved IMG_2206 camera on vertical wall planes: the west wall (x -187, the generated garden-wall line, which projects onto it) stands 1.9 m with a 1.0 m gate centred at z 31.1; the east wall runs from about (-183.1, 30.1) south-south-east past its gate (centred at (-182.37, 31.22)) towards the block by the camera, the direction on which that gate measures a usual 0.88 m wide and the wall top falls towards the camera as photographed (IMG_2208 shows the same wall). Estimated: the walls' ends and the patio's north and south sides, which are unseen.

edges.note: East wall with the second brown gate (IMG_2206 x 695-735), running south-south-east from about (-183.1, 30.1); direction measured from the gate's width and the wall top's fall in IMG_2206, matching IMG_2208; its ends are estimated.
West wall with the first brown gate (IMG_2206 x 540-605): cap 1.9 m, gate 1.0 m wide centred at z 31.08, measured on the wall plane x -187 through the solved camera.

surfaces.name: Calle Isabel · crazy paving from the lawn to the iron gate and the east block
surfaces.note: Photo-supported (IMG_2205 x 850-1200, y 600-700): continuous irregular pale stone paving from the lawn's east edge right up to the iron gate's foot (cast at about (-162.55..-161.8, 7.2-7.5)) and along the east block's face, where the model had the lane's terracotta squares and a generated wall and hedge. Raised over the lane mesh as the Calle Isabel paving is. Estimated: its south end, hidden by the yucca and the tree.

surfaces.name: North pool south-west · tiled connector towards Calle Pintor Dalí

edges.note: Low white curbs and a curved approach are photographed at the Dalí-side mouth; only the first 10 m of the connector receives them. The exact endpoints are estimates.

surfaces.note: Ground-level IMG_2551/2552 face the Dalí junction and show a square terracotta-tiled approach, low white kerbs and planting; IMG_2553/2706/2707 face east along the same tiled link between house fronts. The full centreline is an estimated corridor following the free space between unchanged registry footprints, bending around the west side of the photographed gated patio and meeting the existing north-pool south-west crazy-paving path at (-179.7, 31.3). The phones' camera pins disagree with the building polygons by several metres, so this is provisional plan geometry, NOT a solved-camera or surveyed trace. Do not infer public access through private gates, unseen walls or house footprints. Verify the path ends, widths and corner shape against additional ground-level photos before placement approval.
